issues.failure_explanation: For the linear SDE dU=(AU+a)dt+sqrt(2C)dW the covariance obeys dΣ/dt = AΣ_t + Σ_t A^T + 2C, with A = -(γ/κ)(I - (β/κ)P_t C^{-1}). Since A^T = -(γ/κ)(I - (β/κ)C^{-1}P_t), the last bracket term should be Σ_t C^{-1}P_t, not Σ_t P_t C^{-1}. These coincide only if P_t and C_{*,t} commute. That fails, e.g., for C=K, or for C=Σ_t when Σ_t does not commute with Σ. In those cases the stated dΣ_t/dt is not even symmetric, so the stated evolution equation is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Σ_t P_t C_{*,t}^{-1} by Σ_t C_{*,t}^{-1} P_t, i.e. take the transpose correctly in the proof and in the statement.
issues.overall_effect: The general moment ODE stated in the lemma is wrong outside commuting cases. Its later uses (the corollary at Σ_t=Σ and the CBS-equivalence lemma, where P_t C^{-1} is a scalar multiple of I) only invoke commuting cases and remain valid.
issues.title: Covariance ODE omits a transpose and is non-symmetric when P_t and C_{*,t} do not commute
issues.why_classification: A one-term local correction of a standard formula. No downstream result or claim changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a weighted covariance $\mathbf C_{U,t} = \mathcal C_{\alpha, \lambda \mathcal C(\rho_t)}(\rho_t; U_t)$ with scalars $\alpha\ge0$ and $\lambda > 0$.
For any choice of the CBS parameter

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma allows any α>0, but λ = α'/(α-α') is undefined when α=α' and negative when α<α'. The weighted-covariance preconditioner, and hence the localized CBS dynamics it refers to, is defined only for λ>0. For λ<0 the distance weight exp(-||v-u||^2/(2λ)) grows, so the preconditioner is not a valid localized covariance in general. The statement therefore asserts equivalence for parameter choices that do not define the method.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require α>α', or treat α=α' as λ=∞ (weighted covariance C_α). The proof is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The equivalence is established only for α>α' (with α=α' read as λ=∞, i.e. the C_α preconditioner). The quantifier 'α>0' overstates it.
issues.title: CBS-equivalence uses λ outside the allowed range (λ ≤ 0 or undefined) for α ≤ α'
issues.why_classification: Adding the local condition α>α' keeps the conclusion and its purpose, since α remains a free parameter.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it holds that $m_t = m'_{ct}$ and $\Sigma_t = \Sigma'_{ct}$ with

issues.failure_explanation: The listed parameters fix α, κ, β and λ but not γ. The localized CBS moment ODEs scale with γ, so m_t = m'_{ct} and Σ_t = Σ'_{ct} hold only for γ = 2α'/(α'+1), the value obtained from the corollary's formula for the weighted covariance. The proof silently assumes this value, so the statement as written is false for other γ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add γ = 2α'/(α'+1) (equivalently, γ from eq:cor:lcbs:gauss:gamma:gamma-Cw) to the lemma's parameter list.
issues.overall_effect: The equivalence claim is unsupported as stated for arbitrary γ.
issues.title: CBS-equivalence statement omits the required value of γ
issues.why_classification: Stating the hypothesis the proof already uses is a local repair with no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this paper we always choose $\alpha=0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The drift mean is meant to approximate μ_{β,κC/β}, whose weights are exp(-β||v-u||^2_{κC}/2) π̂(v)^β. The algorithm instead uses w_{α,λĈ}, i.e. the preconditioner's localization parameters. Because the paper always takes α=0, the literal drift is a purely distance-weighted mean with no dependence on π̂. The discretized dynamics in eq:comput:lcbs-alg then do not approximate eq:lcbs:loc-prec:lcbs and cannot target π.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace w_{α,λĈ}^{ij} by w_{β,κĈ/β}^{ij} in both sums of eq:particle:mu-batch.
issues.overall_effect: The practical algorithm as written does not implement the mean-field localized CBS drift.
issues.title: Random-batch drift mean uses the preconditioner weights w_{α,λĈ} instead of w_{β,κĈ/β}
issues.why_classification: The correct weights are fixed by the left-hand-side notation, so the fix is a local substitution with no change to the method or its claims.
